report: Checked all 25 candidate lemmas across the 11 verses; every difference in treatment is licensed by the ASV's own English rather than a split in analysis.

Construct chains with an arthrous rectum rendered anarthrously (the God of heaven 1.2, the house of God 1.4, the heads of fathers houses 1.5) all front the single the to the article and leave the construct bare; chains with a bare proper-name rectum (the house of Jehovah 1.3, 1.5, 1.7; the God of Israel 1.3) all supply the the on the construct; the earth 1.2 is the arthrous case and counts two thes. Consistent under rule 29 throughout.

Standalone הָאֱלֹהִים rendered bare God (1.3, 1.5) leaves the article unrepresented in both places; הַמְּקֹמוֹת → any place (1.4) gives the determiner to כֹּל and leaves the article nothing, matching rule 41's limit.

The formula אֲשֶׁר בִּ + place → which is in X (1.2, 1.3 twice, 1.4, 1.5) puts the copula on the preposition every time (rule 49); the adjunct בִּירוּשָׁלִַם of build ... in Jerusalem (1.2) takes a bare in. Licensed, not a split.

Waw renderings (Now, so that, and, Then, Also, even) each follow the ASV's written connective; the one supplied and in 1.10 (other vessels) has no waw and is correctly added. Object suffixes: ם of וַיִּתְּנֵם (1.7) is unrepresented because the ASV writes had put with no pronoun, while 1.8's suffixes take those and them as written.

The two added units (put it 1.1; and 1.10) are the only supplied English no morpheme licenses; every other supplied word (there is 1.3, they that were 1.6, they of 1.11, houses 1.5, offering 1.4, things 1.6, sort 1.10) is placed by the rule that licenses it.

BSB disagreements: all are documented convention (unrendered prepositions לֵאמֹר/dative לִי/עָלַי; articles the ASV writes no the for in 1.3, 1.4, 1.5; the unrendered object suffix in 1.7). None is a genuine error. The 1.3 margin (the God who is in Jerusalem) was read and set aside per rule 38.
No convention needed: the six repeated notes each restate a contract rule (12, 15, 16, 19, 29, 49). Nothing in this chapter generalises beyond the contract as it stands.
